To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the development of cross veins in Drosophia involves three distinct signaling processes and that insects can independently regulate cross vein structure at each of these three stages.

(1) crossveins are a complex structure that develops in stages, and (2) the development and evolution in the number, placement and flexibility of crossveins are mediated by different signalling pathways.

the number and location of the crossvein primordia in the wing imaginal disc is determined by signalling from the cdc42‐JNK signal transduction pathway; the crossveins are induced to form in the disc by signalling from the dorsal wing epidermis; and the crossveins form in the disc in response to signalling from the EFG‐receptor–MAP Kinase pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evolution crossveins in insects.
the development and evolution, in the context of a specific developmental process, the formation of cross‐veins in insect flight wings.
understanding the genetic basis for the development and evolution in insect wings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of cross‐veins in D. melanogaster involves at least three distinct signalling processes that interact to specify the number, location and structure of these veins.
crossvein evolution is the result of the evolution of the developmental mechanisms that regulate crossvein development.
the crossvein pattern of the wing is determined by a series of interlocking signalling events, each of which is subject to independent modulation by genetic and environmental factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
crossveins are formed in a 3‐stage process, with each stage involving the interaction of a specific signalling pathway with the EGF‐Receptor‐MAP Kinase signalling pathway.
crossveins in the wings of insects are formed by a series of signalling interactions between different parts of the wing epithelium.

the formation of cross‐veins in D. melanogaster involves the integration of multiple signalling pathways, and that this integration may account for the ability of crossveins to evolve independently in different insect lineages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
crossveins are formed in three stages.
the development of the crossvein is a highly regulated process involving the interaction of several different signalling pathways.
the formation of a crossvein is not just a matter of cell death, but rather a process in which the crossvein forms in response to a series of signalling events.
